sections.research_extension: Boffetta and Ecke 2012: 2D turbulence never strictly realized but approximates large-scale atmosphere and oceans (p. 428); enstrophy bound dZ/dt = -2 nu P, energy dissipation vanishes as nu -> 0, inverse energy cascade, contrast with 3D vortex stretching (p. 430).
sections.teaching_construction: Baroclinic term shown to vanish only for constant density; material-line equation (6.19) and the Cauchy-type correspondence for nu = 0; enstrophy equation (6.20); 2D enstrophy bound (6.21) derived; running-case vorticity ratio 117.

sections.section: Rates of strain and rotation

sections.research_extension: Hunt, Wray and Moin 1988 (p. 196, eqs. 2.1-2.2): II = du_i/dx_j du_j/dx_i = E_ij^2 - omega_i^2/2; eddy zones where II < -II_E, plus a pressure-minimum criterion.
sections.teaching_construction: Sign check of (6.24) and its inverse; pseudovector argument with det(a); (omega.grad)U = S omega and the stretching/tilting split; Poisson right side as S:S - |omega|^2/2 (6.26) with rigid-rotation and plane-strain limit checks; box-average balance (6.27) and eps = nu <omega'^2> for homogeneous fluctuations; running-case rms vorticity 2.3e3 1/s.

sections.teaching_construction: Scaled pressure and the scalar's 1/(Re Sc); three boundaries (model approximations, identical scaled data, statistics for turbulent flows); half-scale air model at Ma = 0.33.

sections.section: Invariance under changes of frame and time reversal

sections.teaching_construction: Chain-rule proof of Galilean invariance (6.31); accelerating frame absorbed into pressure; derivation of the rotating-frame equation (6.32) from the rotation of frame-fixed vectors, with Coriolis and centrifugal terms; link to chapter 5's Coriolis parameter; Table 6.1.

sections.section: Irrotational fluctuations: the Corrsin-Kistler result
sections.lecture_material: Irrotational flow: zero vorticity; derivation of d<u_iu_j>/dx_i = dk/dx_j (Corrsin Kistler equation, slide f0004); Reynolds stress acts like an isotropic stress; turbulence is rotational.
sections.research_extension: Corrsin and Kistler 1955, NACA Report 1244, p. 15 (PDF p. 18), eqs. (23)-(25) and the following sentences: no net apparent shear forces; the tensor need not have only diagonal terms.
sections.teaching_construction: Index steps of the derivation; condition on a_ij compatible with (9.21); qualification of the lecture's 'only isotropic effect'.

sections.section: Reflection symmetries of the Reynolds stresses
sections.lecture_material: Statistically 2D flow invariant under x_3 reflection: <U_3> = <u_1u_3> = <u_2u_3> = 0; channel symmetric about x_2 = 0.
sections.research_extension: Lee-Moser data: max |<u_1u_3>+| = 4.9e-3, |<u_2u_3>+| = 4.7e-4 against 0.903; max |W+| = 8.6e-3 (3.8e-4 of the centreline velocity); header calls them quality indicators.
sections.teaching_construction: Derivation from the PDF; correction of the (2,2) slide entry and of the conclusion that only normal stresses remain; <U_2> = 0 attributed to continuity.

sections.section: The mean scalar equation and the scalar flux
sections.lecture_material: Scalar decomposition; averaged scalar equation; turbulent scalar flux; scalar closure problem; temperature as an example.
sections.teaching_construction: Unit of the flux; count of new unknowns.

sections.section: The gradient-diffusion hypothesis
sections.lecture_material: Hypothesis <u phi'> = -Gamma_T grad<phi>; effective diffusivity; flow property not fluid property; used by almost every turbulence model (lecture's judgement).
sections.research_extension: Milani, Ling, Eaton 2020 (arXiv v2): p. 1 two types of counter-gradient transport in an inclined jet in crossflow and a stable tensor diffusivity; p. 3 definition and earlier reports; pp. 8-9 near-wall type with both v'c' and dc/dy positive and pressure-scalar correlation.
sections.teaching_construction: Separation of the alignment and sign claims; ill-posedness of Gamma_eff < 0 (growth rate |Gamma_eff| kappa^2); link to chapter 4's K.

sections.section: The turbulent-viscosity hypothesis
sections.lecture_material: Boussinesq 1877 (lecture's attribution); analogy with the Newtonian stress; deviatoric Reynolds stress proportional to the mean strain rate; nu_eff; modified pressure; five components related through nu_T.
sections.research_extension: Schmitt 2007 (HAL preprint pp. 3-4): 1877 publication reporting an 1872 Academy meeting; Reynolds 1895; tensorial form of Boussinesq's expressions.
sections.teaching_construction: Why the deviatoric part is required (trace argument); alignment of principal axes; reduction of unknowns to nu_T and Gamma_T.

sections.section: Shear-flow forms, scaling, and what the hypothesis leaves open
sections.lecture_material: Boundary-layer forms with opposite signs; specifying nu_T and Gamma_T solves the closure; nu_T and Gamma_T scale with the flow and grow linearly with Re away from walls; Pr_T approximately 1; data contradict the hypothesis but it is the simplest closure.
sections.teaching_construction: Evaluation of nu_T from the DNS; quantitative test of the Re-scaling statement; link to (4.13).

sections.section: Testing the turbulent-viscosity hypothesis on the channel

sections.research_extension: Schmitt 2007: indicator and 0.86 threshold (p. 6), databases (pp. 6-7), total-stress alignment poor for 3 < y+ < 70 with minimum at y+ = 10.5 +/- 0.5 (p. 8), annular-pipe point with S = 0 and R non-zero (p. 8), 'almost never verified' (p. 1), mean fields versus second moments (p. 10). Lee-Moser data: b_11 0.13-0.51, b_22 -0.33 to -0.06; gamma_aS turbulent 0.013 to at most 0.59; total 0.996 at y+ 1, below 0.86 beyond y+ 2.9, near-wall minimum 0.23 at y+ 14, 0.018 near the centreplane. Lee-Moser data at Re_tau 543 and 5186: minimum of gamma_aS with viscous stress at y+ = 13.8 (0.238) and 14.8 (0.209); running case max <u_1^2>+ = 8.10 at y+ = 15.2, one grid point from the minimum.
sections.teaching_construction: TVH prediction of isotropic normal stresses in simple shear; gamma_aS for the channel reduces to sqrt(2)|<uv>|/|a|; Figure 9.2.

sections.section: The objects of the chapter and the running case
sections.lecture_material: Symbols u(l), tau(l), l_0, u_0, Re, Re_0 from the slides.
sections.teaching_construction: Formal model of flow scales and eddy scales; continuation of the air jet of chapters 6-8 with the atmospheric layer of chapter 5 as contrast; notation Re_0 versus Re(l).

sections.section: Turbulent motions span a range of sizes that widens with the Reynolds number
sections.lecture_material: Laminar flow has one characteristic length (1 cm jet example); turbulent motions range from the flow width delta to much smaller scales that shrink as Re increases; continuum still valid; Re 1e5 versus 1e10 illustration.
sections.teaching_construction: Factor 5.6e3 from Re^(-3/4) with its assumptions; Knudsen number from chapter 6.

sections.section: Richardson's energy cascade: inviscid transfer and viscous dissipation
sections.lecture_material: Richardson (1922) cascade idea; production at the largest scales; transfer by inviscid processes; dissipation by viscosity; Navier-Stokes inertia term breaks up large scales, viscous term dominant at small scales; Kolmogorov (1941) quantified the picture.
sections.research_extension: Richardson 1922, p. 66: 'big whirls have little whirls...' in the context of cumulus convection and a single eddy coefficient.
sections.teaching_construction: Proof (10.1)-(10.2) that inertia and pressure terms conserve energy in a periodic box; triad identity (10.3); statement that neither proves direction or locality of transfer.

sections.section: Eddies, their scales and the Reynolds number of the largest eddies
sections.lecture_material: Re = U L/nu known before the flow; eddy definition; u(l), tau(l) = l/u(l); l_0 comparable to L; u_0 of order u' = (2k/3)^(1/2) comparable to U; Re_0 = u_0 l_0/nu large, viscous effects negligible.
sections.teaching_construction: Origin of the factor 2/3 via (8.25); local flow scales in a developing jet (factor 28); Re_0^(-1) = 7.3e-5 via (5.17).

sections.section: The dissipation rate is set by the largest eddies
sections.lecture_material: Richardson's notion of unstable eddies; cascade continues until Re small; epsilon ~ u_0^2/tau_0 = u_0^3/l_0 set by the first step; consistent with observations in free shear flows where epsilon is independent of nu.
sections.research_extension: McComb et al. 2015: epsilon = C_eps U^3/L (p. 2), Batchelor 1953 and Sreenivasan 1984 attributions (p. 2), C_eps = C_eps,inf + C/R_L with 0.468 +/- 0.006 and 18.9 +/- 1.3 up to R_L = 5875 (p. 1).
sections.teaching_construction: Exact dimensional form (10.6); pipeline argument for why the first step sets the rate; running-case C_eps = 0.4694 and 0.3 % change per factor 2 in nu; correction of the board tau_0.

sections.section: The hypothesis of local isotropy
sections.lecture_material: Two questions (size of smallest eddies; trend of u(l), tau(l)); three hypotheses premised on decreasing u(l), tau(l); large eddies anisotropic and affected by BCs; directional bias lost; hypothesis of local isotropy at sufficiently high Re for l << l_0; 'sufficiently high Re' emphasized.
sections.research_extension: Kolmogorov 1941, Definitions 1-2 (pp. 9-10), likelihood statement, domain conditions, cannot be rigorously proved, Taylor isotropy confirmed only for grid turbulence (p. 10). Schumacher, Sreenivasan, Yeung (arXiv pp. 1-2): skewness of du/dy falls off less steeply than 1/R_lambda; hyperskewness not perceptibly diminished at R_lambda 1000; Shen and Warhaft seventh moment increases; their reading that this need not imply persistent anisotropy.
sections.teaching_construction: Reflection proof (10.8) that odd moments of a transverse derivative vanish under local isotropy; application to the jet.

sections.section: A demarcation length and the loss of the flow's geometry
sections.lecture_material: l_EI ~ l_0/6 (nominal); anisotropic large and isotropic small eddies; geometry of large eddies lost; universality; zoom-in illustration jet versus channel versus cylinder.
sections.teaching_construction: Running-case l_EI values; distinction between pictures and statistics.

sections.section: Transfer, dissipation and the first similarity hypothesis
sections.lecture_material: Two dominant processes: transfer rate T_EI and viscous dissipation; epsilon ~ T_EI; first similarity hypothesis; Kolmogorov scales; identities Re_eta = 1 and epsilon = nu (u_eta/eta)^2 = nu/tau_eta^2; Kolmogorov scales characterize the dissipative eddies.
sections.research_extension: Kolmogorov 1941, p. 12: first hypothesis of similarity in his words.
sections.teaching_construction: Small-scale energy budget (10.9) for homogeneous turbulence, with the large-scale dissipation bounded by Re(l_EI)^-1 = 8.0e-4 for the jet, (transport term needed and not estimated for the jet) and departure estimate (10.10) with decaying-grid-turbulence value 0.2; universal-function form (10.11); exact mean-square strain (10.13) and running-case value 1.65e3 1/s.

sections.section: In Kolmogorov units the small scales of different flows are statistically identical
sections.lecture_material: y = (x - x_0)/eta, w(y) = [U(x,t_0) - U(x_0,t_0)]/u_eta; statistically isotropic and identical for |y| < l_EI/eta; statistically similar, identical when scaled.
sections.research_extension: Kolmogorov 1941, p. 9 (moving coordinates) and p. 12 (eqs. 15-18, rescaling to unit viscosity and dissipation).
sections.teaching_construction: Statement in terms of the N-point PDF (8.23); jet versus ABL conversions (127 eta and 3.0 eta per cm; u_eta ratio 41; |y| = 20 lengths; bound ratio 240).

sections.section: The ratios of the smallest to the largest scales
sections.lecture_material: Ratios from the definitions and epsilon ~ u_0^3/l_0; derivation of eta/l_0 ~ Re^(-3/4).
sections.teaching_construction: Back-reference to (5.18) without re-derivation; constants C_eps kept; statement that the ratios need the empirical scaling; running-case values.

sections.section: The ratios of the smallest to the largest scales (continued)
sections.lecture_material: Recap of the first similarity hypothesis and identities; derivations of u_eta/u_0 ~ Re^(-1/4) and tau_eta/tau_0 ~ Re^(-1/2); smallest scales very small compared with largest; separation widens with Re.
sections.teaching_construction: As above.

sections.section: The second similarity hypothesis
sections.lecture_material: Range l_0 >> l >> eta; Re of these eddies large; second similarity hypothesis (determined by epsilon, independent of nu).
sections.research_extension: Kolmogorov 1941, p. 12: second hypothesis of similarity in his words (lower bound only) and its footnote; p. 13, eqs. 22-23: B_dd(r) ~ C eps^(2/3) r^(2/3) with an absolute constant.
sections.teaching_construction: Unique exponents (10.16) with undetermined constant; consistency of the two hypotheses (Phi(x) -> C_u x^(1/3)).

sections.section: The energy-containing range, the inertial subrange and the dissipation range
sections.lecture_material: l_DI = 60 eta (nominal); universal equilibrium range split into inertial subrange and dissipation range; energy-containing range l_0/6 < l < 6 l_0; slide figure of eddy-size ranges.
sections.teaching_construction: Figure 10.1 computed for jet and ABL; existence condition (10.17) with thresholds 2.56e3 and 5.5e4 (C_eps = 1), 3.30e3 and 7.1e4 (C_eps = 0.468); jet 0.55 decades, ABL 2.9 decades; sensitivity to the nominal factors.

sections.section: Velocity and time scales in the inertial subrange
sections.lecture_material: u(l) = (eps l)^(1/3) = u_eta (l/eta)^(1/3) ~ u_0 (l/l_0)^(1/3); tau(l) = (l^2/eps)^(1/3) = tau_eta (l/eta)^(2/3) ~ tau_0 (l/l_0)^(2/3); board elimination of nu; u(l) and tau(l) decrease as l decreases.
sections.teaching_construction: Constant-transfer identity (10.20); end-value identities; eddy Reynolds number (10.21) with Re(l_DI) = 235; running-case velocities and times; gradient scaling l^(-2/3).
